metadata.coordinate_system: SVG viewBox (1200x800) — use CRS.Simple in Leaflet with Y-inversion
metadata.description: Spatial data for the continent of Veydria. Coordinates from coordinate-manifest.yaml; topology from veydria-topology.yaml.

properties.name: Aethelian Basin
properties.description: A three-day sail across. Six port cities stand on its shores, four great free ports and two lesser harbours. They do not make war on one another, and they do not trust one another. The Basin grows no grain, mines no metal, swears no oath of its own; it certifies. The triple-seal excommunication, by which a captain's name is read aloud at each of the six customs-houses, has in the memory of the older clerks brought four houses to ruin and one master to suicide. The water is shallow and forgiving. The credit is long-memoried. The rim ports lie about a day's coasting apart: Tavakh-Qarat to Halani-Tamu is a single day along the north-east shore, the short hop the cool-season credit traffic makes between settlements, against the three days of the open sail straight across.
properties.opening: The Basin's mouth faces west toward the open ocean. Halkar Straits is the narrow passage at the mouth. The Oravan archipelago lies beyond (west of) the straits in the open ocean. Ships entering the Basin from Oravan pass through Halkar Straits eastward into the enclosed sea

properties.name: Ngaru Bon
properties.elevation: Vertically zoned (ADR-0047 D1): inhabited miombo shelf 1200-2000m; hypoxic crown 3500-4800m (peaks to ~6000m, no habitation above ~5000m)
properties.terrain: Wooded highveld shelf, where the people, fields, forges and copperbelt lie, walled above by a cold hypoxic crown of dzongs, sacred lakes and the Lam-Chen crossing. Tsetse belts close the lower approaches
properties.basin_access: Indirect — via Lam-Chen Pass to steppe, then overland to Basin; or via the southeastern route: porters through the tsetse foothills to Smith-Spring, Irrah caravans down the Southern Thread to Khulut, then Dzong-Tamu on the Basin's southeastern margin (Kilwa analog; a bypass of the Lam-Chen/A-Tzalan corridor)
borders: kheshkai (south, via Lam-Chen Pass — singular exit)

properties.name: Irrah
properties.cardinal: Two lobes (climate spine Ruling 7): a northern lobe east of the Basin, between Ngaru-Bon and Kheshkai's west flank; a southeastern lobe on the frankincense coast, east of the Ndjadi floodplain
properties.elevation: Variable — sabkha flats near sea level, oasis valleys 200-800m, frankincense escarpments to 1500m
properties.terrain: Arid desert in two lobes, parted by Kheshkai's wall and the Ndjadi floodplain. Northern lobe: gravel plains under Ngaru-Bon's tsetse foothills, erg toward the Basin, a semiarid margin along Kheshkai's west flank, narrowing south to the delta's head at Khulut. Southeastern lobe: thorn-steppe and the frankincense escarpments, beyond a low eastern divide from the floodplain. Three trunk corridors (Northern Thread, Southern Thread, The Spine) connect 40+ oases in the northern lobe; the frankincense crossing joins the lobes (veydria-climate-spine.md)
properties.basin_access: Via caravan routes westward to Basin's eastern shore (Halani-Tamu port); Scribal Ladder pilgrimage route connects south to Ndjadi delta via Basin transit
borders: ngaru_bon (north of the northern lobe, at the Smith-Spring frontier below the tsetse foothills)
kheshkai (east of the northern lobe, along the west flank; north of the southeastern lobe, a lower, drier margin beyond the wall's end)
ndjadi (the northern lobe reaches the delta's head at Khulut; the southeastern lobe lies over the low eastern divide)
aethelian_basin (west of the northern lobe, caravan terminus at Halani-Tamu)

properties.name: Kheshkai
properties.elevation: Rising plateau (ADR-0048 D4): southern lip 2000-2500m over the Ndjadi floodplain, climbing to 3500-4500m in the interior
properties.terrain: High-altitude grassland steppe with cliff edges overlooking Ndjadi delta to south. The dzud and the deep winters belong to the high interior, in the rain shadow of the southern wall
properties.basin_access: Overland to eastern Basin ports; also via A-Tzalan Ford to Ndjadi delta
borders: irrah (west, the northern lobe along the flank; south, the southeastern lobe beyond the wall's end)
ndjadi (south, via A-Tzalan Ford — cliff edge descends to delta)
qollari (southwest, at Breath-of-Cloud sanctuary — cloud forest meets steppe)

properties.name: Ndjadi
properties.terrain: Tropical monsoon river delta at Bengal latitude (ADR-0048 D6) with five distributaries, stone barays, mangrove swamps
properties.basin_access: Direct — delta mouth enters Basin's south shore (Ki-Mbuhari port zone)
borders: qollari (west, Qollari cliff roads descend to floodplains)
irrah (north, the northern lobe at Khulut; east, the southeastern lobe over the low eastern divide)

properties.name: Qollari
properties.terrain: Cloud forest and mountain terraces with carved cliff roads, fog banks, astronomical observatories
properties.basin_access: Via cliff roads descending to Oravan coast and Basin's southern rim
borders: ndjadi (east, cliff roads descend to floodplains)
oravan (west, cliff roads descend to coast)

properties.name: Oravan
properties.cardinal: West (archipelago in open ocean, facing Basin entrance)
properties.terrain: Volcanic island chain with narrow straits, coral reefs, geothermal vents
properties.basin_access: Via Halkar Straits into Basin's western opening
borders: qollari (east, via Gold-Banner Route — maritime to mountain)

properties.name: Lam Chen Pass
properties.description: One road. Three days under cliff and a day in scree, with no shelter that a determined Council cannot find. Ngaru-Bon depends on the pass for the trade that feeds the plateau; Kheshkai prospers on the traffic that crosses it. The pass has changed hands six times in living memory, and never for long. The first thaw belongs to whoever wintered above, and the wintering above kills men. The widow-tax at the Smith-Spring side is collected by a Khen-Po whose name is not written in the register.
properties.strategic_value: Closure creates existential famine on the Ngaru-Bon crown (dzongs, councils, pass-garrisons) within one growing season. The shelf feeds itself but cannot lift bulk grain onto the crown without pack animals, which the tsetse belts deny it (ADR-0047 D1)

properties.name: A Tzalan Ford
properties.description: Where the Kheshkai cliff edge descends to the Ndjadi delta. The ford is two pole-lengths deep at low water and impassable at flood, and for two of the four seasons the only crossing is the seizure of one bank by whichever clan-lord can hold it. Kosh-Taka held it once and held the upstream weirs with it; the delta starved through three growing seasons. The toll is paid in unminted copper, weighed at the ford by a Kheshkai factor who answers to no court the delta recognizes.
properties.strategic_value: Seizure controls north-south overland trade. The weirs just above the ford stand in Ki-Njia, a Ndjadi treaty water-precinct on steppe ground: a weir release can drown the crossing against a hostile holder, and whoever seizes ford and precinct together can starve the delta. Below the ford, the Ki-Jenga cut can take the dry-season flow off the flood-flats at the escarpment foot (ADR-0047 D3)

properties.name: Qollari Cliff Roads
properties.description: The carved descent from the cloud forest takes four days for a loaded llama and six for a sick one. The roads narrow at the upper switchbacks to a man's reach plus a finger, which is the width the calendar-keepers want; the load cap is twenty-five to thirty kilo by ordinance and by what the animal will bear. The cliff-engineers' guild at the Apu-Yana waystation can collapse a half-stade of switchback by removing four wedge-stones, and have done so twice in the memory of the living roadmasters.
properties.strategic_value: Qollari monopoly on highland-lowland access. Llama 25-30 kg load cap forces dense waystation networks

properties.name: Halkar Straits
properties.description: The strait is half a march wide at its narrowest. Every Oravan keel that enters the Basin passes through it, and every obsidian shipment in continental commerce passes through it twice, once north and once south. The Halkar pilot-houses are Oravan, the harbor-fees are Oravan, the rates are Oravan, and the Basin ports settle the books at Tavakh-Qarat in the cool season. Three captains in the last cycle preferred the open ocean and the monsoon to the pilot-house. They have not been heard from.
properties.strategic_value: Oravan naval dominance is absolute in the Basin but cannot enforce land control without allies

properties.name: Smith Spring
properties.description: The hot spring rises ore-bearing at the Ngaru-Bon margin and flows three leagues south before the iron is exhausted from the water. The Ngaru-Bon forge-precinct holds the upstream stones; the Irrah salt-collectors hold the downstream pans; the Basin's caravan-masters hold the buffer-riverbank by a working truce no court has authored. Iron and charcoal travel south at the price the season's hostage-children fix. Salt travels north. A factor who proposes a written treaty for the buffer is asked, politely, to leave.
properties.strategic_value: Shared resource that forces cooperation. Iron and charcoal flow south; salt flows north

properties.name: Breath of Cloud
properties.description: Where the steppe meets cloud forest at the only joint cross-civ sanctuary on the continent. The Kheshkai shamans and the Qollari calendarists convene every third year and the festival-towns swell to a season's bulk in eight days. In the off years the border is a dirt track watched by a single Khen-Po. The Khazadari rate-house at the senior festival town fails twice in three rotations and recapitalizes itself by a method the Inner Circle has chosen not to publish. The wool-trade depends on the festival year falling.
properties.strategic_value: Massive commercial traffic during festival years creates boom-bust cycle in border towns

properties.name: Ki-Mbuhari
properties.etymology: Ndjadi: Ki- (settlement) + Mbu- (water) + hari 'surplus'. The Surplus-Water Settlement
properties.location: South shore, where Ndjadi delta enters
properties.function: The south-shore grain port, where the Ndjadi delta enters the Basin and where the High Granaries' evaporative-cooled stores feed the continental circuit. The Darb caravan-staging quarter on the south side pays no substrate-cistern levy, and the Court of the Three Mouths has chosen, in three reviews, not to revisit the question. The Imajīn caravan-mistresses hold the leverage.

properties.name: Tavakh-Qarat
properties.etymology: Mixed Basin pidgin: tavakh (Irrah-derived 'exchange, balance') + qarat (Irrah 'citadel'). The Exchange Citadel
properties.function: The north-shore port and the oldest commercial quarter. Inside the pale-gold limestone arcades the Khazadari Inner Circle sets the cross-rate cycle twice a year; the soda-ash glassworks at the periphery kill their senior masters before the fourth cohort can be trained. The Junior Clerks' Association now writes fifteen percent of the port's underwriting at rates the Inner Circle has been silent on for eleven cycles.

properties.name: Halani-Tamu
properties.etymology: Oravan: hala 'reef, harbor' + ni (genitive) + tamu 'sweetwater'. The Sweetwater Harbor
properties.function: The east-shore port and the monsoon switching point, where the Oravan sea-lanes hand off to the Irrah overland routes. The Coral Docks collect the Harbor Covenant's wave-tithe; the Qalībin Lodges certify the desert-interior escorts; the Bazaar of the Split between them is neutral ground neither core institution claims. The Tin-Aghīz-Lam-Chen partnership absorbs the uncertified gold-work the Inner Council of Ancestor-Smiths chooses not to see.

properties.name: Dzong-Tamu
properties.etymology: Ngaru-Bon: dzong 'fortress-monastery' + tamu (Basin pidgin 'sweetwater/fresh'). The Fortress Harbor
properties.function: The southeast-margin port, link to the Ngaru-Bon highland trade. The Iron Keep and the Click-Market enforce Stone-tithe collection and acoustic-register-gated guild exchange that the Outer Quarters' mixed laborers cannot, on any plausible career path, be admitted to. The Pacha-Urco householders' annual substrate-rite is the only ceremony in which the Click-Market and the periphery share ground.

properties.name: Qhabal Ur
properties.description: The Drowned Step. A monumental stepped platform at the Basin's center, half its steps under water at the high tide and dry at the low. The Oravan post a garrison and the Ndjadi post a scribal-access corps. Both claims rest on use rather than charter, and the Triple-Seal Court has declined to hear a docking dispute three times in the present generation. A captain who lands without one of the two flags loses the cargo to whichever flag posts first.

properties.name: Veyd Kirrha
properties.description: The Ash-Oracle. A volcanic vent on the Basin's southern rim that vents on no schedule the calendar-keepers have been able to resolve. Oravan, Kheshkai, Qollari, and Irrah scholars come to it in rotation, each reading the ash by the lights of his own tradition, and the four readings on a single venting have never agreed. The local Tongue-Guild factor charges by the cycle for the translation work and does not endorse any reading.

properties.name: Aethelian Basin Hub
properties.path_description: Ndjadi delta distributaries → Ki-Mbuhari (south shore) → Basin rim ports (Tavakh-Qarat, Halani-Tamu, Dzong-Tamu); Ngaru-Bon metal in at Dzong-Tamu
properties.commodities: Grain downstream, cotton upstream, Ngaru-Bon metals, re-exported Oravan spices and Irrah salt
properties.bottleneck: Ndjadi river-lords and Aethelian oath-scribes (customs houses; calendar-gated tolls)
properties.consequence_if_closed: Everything. Silting the Basin closes the continent's single clearing house

properties.name: Aethelian Basin Hub
properties.path_description: Ndjadi delta distributaries → Ki-Mbuhari (south shore) → Basin rim ports (Tavakh-Qarat, Halani-Tamu, Dzong-Tamu); Ngaru-Bon metal in at Dzong-Tamu
properties.commodities: Grain downstream, cotton upstream, Ngaru-Bon metals, re-exported Oravan spices and Irrah salt
properties.bottleneck: Ndjadi river-lords and Aethelian oath-scribes (customs houses; calendar-gated tolls)
properties.consequence_if_closed: Everything. Silting the Basin closes the continent's single clearing house

properties.name: Highland-Steppe Corridor
properties.path_description: Two connected legs forming an L-shape: Leg 1 (north-to-south): Ngaru-Bon plateau → Lam-Chen Pass → Kheshkai steppe (metals southbound, horses/tin northbound). Leg 2 (northeast-to-southwest): Kheshkai steppe → Breath-of-Cloud border → Qollari highlands (horses/furs southwestbound, dyes/wool northeastbound)
properties.commodities: Metals, horses, furs, amber, tin, dyes, fine wool. Not a single east-west flow but two bilateral exchanges pivoting through Kheshkai
properties.bottleneck: Kheshkai clan-lords (grazing rights at waystations on both legs)
properties.consequence_if_closed: Ngaru-Bon loses its overland iron market. Qollari loses horse supply and steppe amber. A clan feud can close 300 leagues for a year

properties.name: Highland Relay
properties.path_description: Qollari cloud-state cliff roads → Basin ports and connected lowlands
properties.commodities: High-value low-bulk: medicinals, dyes, ritual barks, fine wool. Also oath-messages (fastest information channel on the continent)
properties.consequence_if_closed: Continental mail slows from weeks to months. Urgent medicinal shipments fail. Calendar schism has historically closed relay for decades

properties.name: Highland Relay
properties.path_description: Qollari cloud-state cliff roads → Basin ports and connected lowlands
properties.commodities: High-value low-bulk: medicinals, dyes, ritual barks, fine wool. Also oath-messages (fastest information channel on the continent)
properties.consequence_if_closed: Continental mail slows from weeks to months. Urgent medicinal shipments fail. Calendar schism has historically closed relay for decades

properties.name: Coastal Monsoon
properties.path_description: Oravan archipelago → Halkar Straits → Basin ports (monsoon-gated circuit)
properties.commodities: Bulk maritime: spices, coral-stone, obsidian, re-exported Irrah dates outbound; iron inbound to archipelago
properties.consequence_if_closed: Oravan imports collapse (no iron = no new ships). Coastal Basin access halves. Monsoon failure or queen-church succession crisis suspends all tithe-backed insurance

properties.name: Caravan Thread
properties.path_description: Three-hub network, not a single thread: Hub 1 (Smith-Spring frontier): Ngaru-Bon iron/charcoal flows south to Irrah; Irrah salt flows north to Ngaru-Bon. This is a frontier contact-point with buffer zone, not a through-route. Hub 2 (Irrah oasis network): internal east-west trunk corridors (The Spine) connecting 40+ oases. Hub 3 (Basin terminus): caravans depart Irrah westward under Qalībin escort to Halani-Tamu port on Basin's east shore
properties.commodities: Salt, frankincense, myrrh, dates, silver outbound from Irrah to Basin; iron, grain, timber, cotton inbound from Basin/Ngaru-Bon to Irrah
properties.bottleneck: Qalībin path-finders (only legally recognized desert escorts for the Basin leg); Smith-Spring buffer zone (neutral contact point for the Ngaru-Bon leg)
properties.consequence_if_closed: Salt supply to southern continent collapses. Irrah iron imports cease. Continental banking network (khatti letters of credit) breaks — Qalībin oath-binders are the de facto banking infrastructure

properties.name: Western Route
properties.path_description: Vaucresne (off-map, west across the open ocean) → Oravan archipelago (Halanimoa clearing-station) → Halkar Straits → Basin ports (Tavakh-Qarat certification)
properties.commodities: Fine paper and other Vaucresne goods inbound, festival-grade powder among them in growing lots; Basin goods outbound
properties.bottleneck: Two necks: Oravan pilot-houses (Halkar Straits) and the Vaucresne rutter
properties.consequence_if_closed: A dozen keels' cargoes a season, and the western gunpowder vector with them (ADR-0044 D1)

properties.name: Copper-for-Steel Road
properties.path_description: Ndjadi delta → A-Tzalan Ford → across Kheshkai steppe → Lam-Chen Pass → Ngaru-Bon plateau
properties.bottleneck: A-Tzalan Ford (Kheshkai can toll/seize) and Lam-Chen Pass (singular exit)
properties.consequence_if_closed: Stopping the treaty is a quarrel over a minority copper share, the steel that rides south under it, and a right the delta has held since before the copperbelt opened. Closing the ford or the pass is another matter: that shuts the first leg of the Highland-Steppe Corridor and threatens the crown's grain (see chokepoints.lam_chen_pass)

properties.name: Zang-Ri (Iron Mountain)
properties.description: Named peak in the Ngaru-Bon plateau. Primary mining site for iron ore; source of the Ngaru-Bon iron and steel monopoly.

properties.name: Apu-Yana (Black Mountain)
properties.description: Active volcanic peak on the Qollari eastern border, near Kheshkai. Sacred site.

properties.name: Volata-Xal ("Shipyard in the Dust")
properties.description: Abandoned Oravan catamaran settlement near A-Tzalan Ford, from the Obsidian Blockade.

properties.name: Halkar
properties.description: Main Oravan port island closest to Halkar Straits. Primary settlement.

properties.name: Kha-Tepet (Blood Mountain)
properties.description: Sacred peak on the Kheshkai steppe. Site of ancestral burial kurgans.

properties.name: Ki-Jenga
properties.description: Inland Ndjadi city. Site of Mbu-Bwana's famous baray from the Obsidian Blockade.

properties.name: Hassag-Nganin (Five-Confluence)
properties.description: Where the five Ndjadi channels braid together. Contested religious site.

properties.name: Wasi-Puma ("House of the Lion")
properties.description: Fortified Qollari settlement built during the Obsidian Blockade.

properties.name: First Caldera
properties.description: Seawater-filled volcanic caldera on an inner Oravan island. Major pilgrimage site.

properties.name: Kelata
properties.description: Obsidian-source island. Key strategic resource for Oravan naval power.

properties.name: Morina
properties.description: Northernmost island of the Oravan chain.

properties.name: Arokar
properties.description: Southernmost island of the Oravan chain.

properties.name: The Neck
properties.description: The lowland gap between Qollari's north-east foothills and the west end of Kheshkai's wall, where the Ndjadi drains north to the Basin.

properties.name: Ngon-Tso
properties.description: Frozen sacred lake on the Ngaru-Bon crown, where the monastic astrologers keep their divination.

properties.name: Lha-Drak
properties.description: Sky-burial cliff and reliquary on the Ngaru-Bon crown.

properties.name: Xal-Tzintla
properties.description: The Dusty Valley: a great depression in the Kheshkai steppe where the herds shelter from winter storms.

properties.name: Great White Sabkha
properties.description: The great white sabkha at Zin-Iferis's edge, where the desert's salt is cut.

properties.name: Central Erg
properties.description: The deep-erg sand sea on the Spine between Qarat al-Fidda and Tin Mashraq. No living oasis lies between the two.

properties.name: Northern Tributary (from Kheshkai)
properties.description: Descends from the Kheshkai escarpment through A-Tzalan Ford.

properties.name: Western Tributary (from Qollari)
properties.description: Flows from Qollari cloud forest into the delta system.

properties.name: Southern Tributary (from Qollari)
properties.description: Flows from the southern Qollari foothills north into the trunk channel.

properties.name: Eastern Trunk
properties.description: Eastern trunk channel gathering the southern tributaries before the distributary fan.

properties.name: Eastern Wall Tributary (from Kheshkai)
properties.description: Descends from the eastern Kheshkai wall into the trunk channel.

properties.name: First Distributary
properties.description: Westernmost channel of the five-distributary fan delta.

properties.name: Second Distributary
properties.description: Second channel, passing near Ki-Jenga.

properties.name: Third Distributary (Central)
properties.description: Central channel — the main navigable waterway.

properties.name: Fourth Distributary
properties.description: Fourth channel, serving the eastern granary districts.

properties.name: Fifth Distributary
properties.description: Easternmost channel, entering the Basin near Dzong-Tamu.

properties.name: Tavakh-Rubāṭ
properties.etymology: Mixed Basin pidgin: tavakh (Irrah-derived 'exchange, balance') + rubāṭ (Irrah 'fortified caravanserai/relay-station'). The Exchange Caravanserai
properties.location: Mid-route sandbar between Basin north shore and Oravan archipelago
properties.function: Bonded grain and obsidian transshipment; monsoon-season crew exchange under queen-church factor

properties.name: Kelata-Tamu
properties.etymology: Oravan: Kelata (obsidian-source island) + tamu 'sweetwater'. The Sweetwater of Kelata
properties.description: Outer Kelata sister-island with a freshwater spring chambered into the lava rock. Obsidian-route pilgrims rest here on the way to First Caldera.

properties.name: Wasi-Pukya
properties.etymology: Qollari: wasi 'house, lineage' + pukya 'spring'. The Spring-House
properties.description: Calendar-keeper waystation midway up the Qollari cliff road. Cistern carved into the rockface; oath-runners change here under calendar-keeper blessing.

properties.name: Dzong-Kha
properties.etymology: Ngaru-Bon dzong 'fortress-monastery' + Kheshkai kha 'blood'. The Fortress of the Blood-Oath
properties.description: Clan-toll waystation at the foot of Lam-Chen Pass. Stone corrals and ice-cellar cisterns; tariff-rolls kept by the closest Kheshkai clan-lord.

properties.name: Tepet-Apu
properties.etymology: Cross-cultural: Kheshkai tepet 'mountain' + Qollari apu 'lord/mountain'. The Mountain-of-Mountains — the two mountain peoples name the truce site each in their own register
properties.description: Mixed-clan waystation on the Breath-of-Cloud descent. Grazing-rights neutral ground; clan-feud truce site under Kheshkai-Qollari oath.

properties.name: Kalli-Xal
properties.etymology: Kheshkai: kalli 'house' + xal 'sand'. The Sand-House — a Kheshkai-attested compound for a steppe relay station
properties.description: Clan-run relay on the Breath-of-Cloud crossing. Grain-pits and corralled mounts kept under a single Kheshkai clan-lord's seal; the grazing toll is settled here before the run to Tepet-Apu. Rations-only resupply: the station hauls grain off the route but cannot offer reliable water beyond what travellers already carry.

properties.name: Zang-Kalli
properties.etymology: Cross-cultural: Ngaru-Bon zang 'iron' + Kheshkai kalli 'house'. The Iron-House — named in both clients' registers for the southbound steel-and-iron leg of the Copper-for-Steel Road (the Ngaru-Bon half of the bilateral trade)
properties.description: Mid-steppe caravanserai between A-Tzalan Ford and Lam-Chen Pass. Run by a Kheshkai sub-clan under Ngaru-Bon factor oversight; ledgers reconcile copper bars northbound against finished steel southbound. Grain stores deep but water carted in.

properties.name: Rubāṭ al-Darb
properties.etymology: Irrah: rubāṭ 'fortified relay-station' (canon architecture term: mudbrick enclosure, central well/cistern, Qalībin garrison) + al-darb (√d-r-b 'road, path'; institution-naming pattern, cf. Sharīf al-Darb). The Waystation of the Road
properties.description: A single rubāṭ fort on the open desert crossing of the Caravan Thread, between Aethelian Basin's eastern ports and the Ngaru-Bon frontier: the only provisioning stop on an otherwise unsupported multi-day traverse. Central cistern, goods storage, and an arcaded animal yard for grain and mounts; Qalībin water-scholar militia (15-25, defensive only) maintain both the stores and the semaphore relay (smoke by day, fire by night).
